solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Made catty remark as setter married without a ring

indicators.note: used in its old sense of 'outside': the setter and married sit around the ring

parts.note: a crossword setter refers to themself as ME
married is WED
a ring is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A newlywed setter makes a spiteful comment about having no wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' does not mean 'lacking' here but 'outside', so O goes inside MEWED.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's cry is a mew or miaow, and a catty remark is jokingly that noise.

clue.text: A group of 9 seen topless and drunk

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
the word seen loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nine people are spotted half-naked and intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts S from SEEN to leave EEN; 'drunk' then shuffles EEN with AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennead is a learned term, from Greek, for a set of nine things or people, like a nonet.

clue.text: Former stand-off in ex-PM's entertaining family

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one name surrounds the other

parts.note: Harold Wilson was a British Prime Minister
family means kin

explanation.surface: A former confrontation inside a former Prime Minister's household.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonny Wilkinson was England's rugby fly-half, a position also called stand-off; 'stand-off' tempts one to think of a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonny Wilkinson played rugby union for England as fly-half, the position also named stand-off half.

clue.text: Dead duck involving shilling for each thug

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the first word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin
per means for each
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dead duck being worth a shilling apiece to a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless violent outlaw, which a thug or ruffian resembles.

clue.text: Wives and girlfriends take ages shopping, having rushed initially to get flannels in LA

indicators.note: take means hold or receive, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: WAGs is the British tabloid term for wives and girlfriends of footballers

indicators.note: the first letters of ages, shopping, having and rushed are used

explanation.surface: Footballers' partners spend ages shopping, then dash to buy flannels in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers all four words before it, not just 'rushed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Washrag is the American word for a face cloth, which the British call a flannel; 'in LA' marks US usage.

clue.text: Celebrations making one traipse around

parts.note: wedding makes two people one

indicators.note: around suggests letters scattered about, here those of traipse

explanation.surface: Festivities that make someone trudge about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one' reads as a link but is a cryptic hint for marrying two people into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedding parties are the festivities held after a marriage ceremony, so celebrations.

clue.text: Beds famous neurologist

definitions.meaning: slang for beds, as in hitting the hay
Oliver ..., author of The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat

explanation.surface: Hospital beds for a celebrated brain doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses this word for a bed, and Oliver Sacks was the British-American neurologist and writer.

clue.text: Department of Surreal Marriages

indicators.note: of signals the letters come from within the following words

explanation.surface: An official body that handles bizarre weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain of activity, as a department is a sphere of responsibility.

clue.text: New e-trading bank

indicators.note: something new is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An online trading bank recently set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank is a slope of ground, and a gradient is an incline or slope.

clue.text: Enveloped in French bosom with pretty big bra size

parts.note: the French for in is en
bosom friends are close friends, so bosom means intimate
D is a fairly large bra cup size

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of an ample French bosom wrapped in a large bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed means surrounded or wrapped up, the same as enveloped.

clue.text: Credit female model for what groom might wear

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Ava is a girl's name
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Credit a female model with styling a bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a formal neckcloth often worn by bridegrooms at weddings.

clue.text: Local resident sporting a tie and V neck top

indicators.note: the top of neck is its first letter
sporting suggests playful frolicking, so the letters frolic into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
V taken as written

explanation.surface: A local wearing a tie with a V-neck jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' reads as 'wearing' but rearranges A TIE, V and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is someone born in a place, so a local inhabitant.

clue.text: Not being able to go off with son getting secretly married instead of daughter in India

definitions.text: Not being able to go off

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another in the word India

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: receiving something hidden inside, so one letter goes into the word son

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A son's secret marriage in India replaces a daughter's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' means fall asleep, not explode or go bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is sleeplessness, the inability to drop off to sleep.

clue.text: United no money for wingers? On the contrary

indicators.note: together with the rest, this says the word money goes without, not with, its outer letters
inverting 'no money for wingers' gives money with no wingers, i.e. its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A football club refusing to pay its wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the other way round: not 'no money for wingers' but 'money with no wingers', MONEY minus M and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To be one is to be united, as in 'we are one'.

clue.text: The gun a girl's used in killing

indicators.note: used here as spent or worn, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The weapon a girl employed in a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughtering is killing, especially killing on a large scale.

clue.text: Looking good on set piece? Header's missed — length (not height) wrong

indicators.note: wrong means amiss or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter, the head, of piece is dropped
H for height is removed from the word length

explanation.surface: A football set piece where the header misses and the length is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header's missed' takes P from PIECE (IECE); 'not height' takes H from LENGTH (LENGT); 'wrong' scrambles IECELENGT.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegenic describes someone who comes across attractively on television, the set here being a TV.

clue.text: Hardy transmitted again around 1.51

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: re-sent means sent again
1 is the Roman numeral I and 51 is LI

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy work broadcast again at 1.51.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist but is the adjective meaning tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient means tough and able to recover, as hardy plants survive harsh weather.

clue.text: Recording male getting married on time? It's short-lived

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
he is a male pronoun
an era is a period of time; on sets it after

explanation.surface: A record of a man marrying in time, which does not last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things of fleeting interest, transient by nature.

clue.text: Views set pieces coming from wing, getting head to second ball first?

parts.note: a ball is round like the letter O
a pinion is a bird's wing
poll is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Football set pieces from the wing: getting a head to the second ball first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is scrambled: 'second ball first' says O goes first; the rest of the football talk is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion polls are surveys that collect a set of people's views.

clue.text: What some brides say, and some widows

indicators.note: some means part of, so the letters lie within the word widows

explanation.surface: The vow uttered by brides, including women marrying again after being widowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The vow given in a wedding ceremony is the words of consent to the marriage.

clue.text: See 5
Tinker with gong, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving one that sounds alike

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

explanation.surface: Fiddling about with a gong.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker with something is to interfere or fiddle with it.

clue.text: Crewmen supply crossing overseas, primarily for the recent immigrant

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the shuffled crew goes around a letter
supply here is the adverb of supple, so the letters bend into a new order
primarily picks the first letter of overseas

explanation.surface: Crew supplying a ship crossing the sea, for a new arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the verb but the adverb from 'supple', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone who has just arrived, such as a recent immigrant.

clue.text: Train company — an endless pain

indicators.note: the end letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A rail firm that is a constant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb, to coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train or tutor them.

clue.text: Wanderer's old mother's benign tumour

parts.note: Wanderer is the setter, so the setter's is my
ma is mother

explanation.surface: The setter's late mother had a harmless growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A myoma is a non-cancerous growth of muscle tissue, such as a fibroid.

clue.text: Set piece from Leeds in last bit of second leg comeback

indicators.note: in places the piece from Leeds inside the reversed letters
a comeback is a return, so the letters run backwards
the final letter of second is taken

parts.note: taken as written
the opening two letters of the city's name are a small piece of it

explanation.surface: A football set piece from Leeds United, staging a second-leg comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set piece' tempts as one football phrase, but 'Set' alone is the definition and 'piece' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelled means set firm, as a jelly sets.

clue.text: Smooth striking ends in the first goal

indicators.note: striking suggests a blow that knocks the letters about
the last letters of the and first are taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A smooth strike puts the opening goal in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks footballing but is the anagram signal; ET from 'the first' joins GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction for playing smoothly with no breaks between notes.

clue.text: Uniform done in another fashion after hotel's suggestion

indicators.note: after puts the uniform and rearranged pieces following the hotel

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: done in another fashion means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel's hint that a uniform be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect insinuation or hint, so a suggestion.

clue.text: Old woman entering shaky ground, beginning to say what Muslim brides might wear

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the old woman goes inside
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: ma is slang for an old woman, a mother

indicators.note: the beginning of say is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mother stepping onto unsteady ground starts to say what brides wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun after 'shaky' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women in public, hence plausible bridal wear.

clue.text: Names around Italy for Florence and Milan?

indicators.note: around shows one piece surrounding another

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention
I is Italy's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Mentions of Italy for two of its famous urban centres.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence is also a girl's name, but here both are Italian places; '?' marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence and Milan are examples of major urban centres, hence large towns.
